review.summary: The core change is correct: the 'members:remove' permission is gone from the admin role in config/teams.php, so only the owner (who holds every permission through the wildcard) can remove people. New tests cover these cases: the owner removes members and admins, admins are refused (403) when they try to remove a member, another admin or the owner, the owner cannot remove themselves, and admins still get the rename and change-role options but not the remove option. However, the diff also removes the 255-character limit on team names in the team update request. Nobody asked for that change. It weakens input validation in the Teams area, so the change cannot be approved as it stands.

findings.summary: An unrequested change removes the 'max:255' rule from the team name. Team names are no longer length-checked. That weakens input validation, and very long names could cause a database error (500) instead of a clear validation message. This is outside the plan and touches team renaming, which is listed under 'Must stay as it is'. Restore the 'max:255' rule.

The old 'owner cannot be removed' test (an admin trying to remove the owner, expecting a validation error) is now a 403 check. That fits the new rules. A new test keeps the owner-self-removal case with the validation error. Nothing is lost, but the change of assertion is worth noting.

The overall verification status is 'unverified' because no protected acceptance tests apply, even though every check passed. The hidden remove option is only tested through the 'can.removeMembers' page flag. The front end itself was not checked.

changes.behavior: Who can remove people from a team
changes.before: Both the team owner and team admins could remove members from the team.
changes.now: Only the team owner can remove members or admins. Admins are refused if they try.

changes.behavior: Remove option on the team settings page
changes.before: Admins saw the option to remove members.
changes.now: Only the team owner sees the remove option. Admins and members do not.

changes.behavior: Length limit on team names when renaming a team
changes.before: A team name could be at most 255 characters. Longer names were rejected with a clear message.
changes.now: Team names have no length limit, so very long names are accepted by the form and may fail with an error when saved. This was not part of the request.

preserved.statement: Admins can still change members' roles.
Admins can still rename the team.
The team owner can still remove members and admins.
The team owner cannot be removed from their own team.
Ordinary members still cannot remove anyone.
Everyone keeps their personal team and can still switch between their teams.
Members can still see the team they belong to.
